messages:
Maya (Finance): FYI we just received a billing escalation from NovaClinic re: their annual renewal invoice RNL-2026-06. They say the platform fee on the renewal is lower than expected and their support tier appears downgraded on the line item.

Tom (AM): NovaClinic closed a support-tier downgrade ticket in our CRM back in Apr but that change was only supposed to take effect on the next billing period. They renewed in Jun for Private deployment + Dedicated capacity. Can you paste the invoice lines?

Sam (Customer Success): Customer sent this screenshot and asked why their renewal total is ~$6k lower than the renewal quote we shared during renewal call. They also said they never requested a retroactive downgrade.

Maya (Finance): Invoice preview snippet from billing system: ```
Invoice: RNL-2026-06
Customer: NovaClinic
Period: 2026-06-01 - 2027-05-31
Lines:
- DEDICATED_CAP_002 Reserved GPU capacity (annual)      $120,000
- PLATFORM_SUBSCRIPTION_ANNUAL  Platform subscription (annual) $18,000
- SUPPORT_TIER_STANDARD  Support - standard (annual)      $6,000
- CONTRACT_DISCOUNT_PROMO  Renewal promo discount                   -$6,000
Total: $138,000
```

Tom (AM): Hmm we had agreed to Support - Premium (annual) at $24k, and platform subscription was locked at $30k per the signed SOW. The invoice shows standard and platform at 18k. That explains the ~$6k delta for platform + big support mismatch.

Rina (Billing Ops): Looking at the billing run logs: renewal engine picks prices from the active contract snapshot. There was a contract snapshot created on 2026-05-15 that incorrectly pulled the old pricing tier (legacy catalog v2) because our price-mapping job failed for that customer due to a missing sku_mapping entry for PRIVATE_PLATFORM_V3. When mapping fails we fallback to catalog default which was 18k.

Maya (Finance): So it's a system undercharge on our side (we owe revenue), but customer is claiming they were underbilled compared to sales quote — they expected higher invoice. We need to decide whether to: 1) reissue corrected invoice to increase charge (not great for customer relations), 2) honor quoted price this cycle and adjust next renewal, or 3) apply a one-time correction or memo. Thoughts?

Sam (Customer Success): Customer is upset about the inconsistency in dates. They explicitly said they didn't authorize a downgrade. Re-issuing an increased invoice will likely frustrate them; we risk churn. Suggest we honor the quoted price this term and record internal remediation to capture lost revenue next quarter.

Ivy (Legal): Contract check: SOW signed 2026-05-20 states platform subscription at $30k and Support - Premium at $24k for the term. Legal preference is to follow contract if it's clear, but forcing an additional charge mid-term is messy. We can escalate to Sales Leadership if we want to pursue collecting the shortfall. Also check whether contract contains pricing error/misrepresentation clauses.

Tom (AM): Sales preference (spoken to lead): keep the customer. We can offer a one-time 'accounting correction' where we honor the renewal at the quoted total and add a surcharge as a separate line next year (or consider amortizing a portion). But we should recover at least part of the delta. Proposal: apply full quoted pricing but credit $12k this term as a concession, then create an internal AR adjustment to track the lost revenue to discuss with FP&A.

Maya (Finance): Operationally, easiest customer-facing approach: 1) Void invoice RNL-2026-06 and reissue RNL-2026-06A with platform=30k and support=premium=24k and apply an "Account Concession" credit of -$12,000 to match the customer's expected total. This preserves their bill amount and keeps contract prices in the ledger. Internally we book a revenue shortfall memo for $12k. Approve?

Rina (Billing Ops): We can void + reissue, but voiding an annual invoice triggers receipts and recognition adjustments. We'll need RevRec to sign off. The billing system can attach an internal memo code INTCORR-295 to the invoice. ETA to reissue: 2 business days after sign-off.

Ivy (Legal): I'm fine with that customer-facing approach. Make sure the reissued invoice references the original and includes the concession text: "Issued to align renewal with quoted SOW; concession applied as customer satisfaction credit." Also capture decision in the legal folder.

Maya (Finance): OK going that route. I'll draft the reissue + credit memo and route to Ivy and RevRec. Also opening ticket for engineering: BF-1899 to fix sku_mapping job fallback so contract snapshots don't default to legacy catalog.

billing-bot: Created ticket TKT-8528 for RNL-2026-06 reissue and linked internal memo INTCORR-295. Patch branch: billing/fix/sku-mapping-fallback-1899 created.

Tom (AM): Please cc me on the customer message. I'll coordinate a one-page note from Sales confirming the SOW pricing and the concession. Sam, please soften messaging with the customer while we reissue.

Sam (Customer Success): Will do. I'll reassure them we'll keep the billed total identical to the quote and share ETA for corrected invoice. :pray:

Maya (Finance): Final note: RevRec flagged that any concession >$10k requires FP&A review; I'm looping in FP&A after legal sign-off. Will update thread when reissue is sent.

Tom (AM): Thanks all, appreciate the quick cross-functional response. :handshake:
